newsitem.title: USA: Race close for TV, Internet coverage of Election Day.
newsitem.headline: Race close for TV, Internet coverage of Election Day.

text.p: The votes are in, and the race between TV and the Internet for the best Election Day coverage was a lot closer than Clinton's landslide victory over Dole.
Election Web sites offered more in-depth information during the day -- if you could get it.

The crush of voters logging on to check returns left some sites virtually inaccessible for hours at a time. No such problems at TV news networks, which were also faster with results and first to call a Clinton victory.

To find out how Net coverage stacked up, we followed several news sites, the candidates' virtual headquarters and one national TV network during the course of the day (all times are Pacific Standard Time):

7 a.m. -- Polls open in California. NBC "Today Show" anchor Katie Couric grills guest pols on Bob Dole's lackluster showing and Clinton's questionable ties to foreign special interests. Co-host Bryant Gumbel summarizes key campaign issues with other NBC reporters.

7:45 a.m. -- PoliticsNow (http://www.politicsnow.com/), the mega-campaign site created by ABC News, the Los Angeles Times, National Journal, Newsweek and the Washington Post, begins with news and pictures from the candidates' last 24 hours on the stump, statistics from newest polls, newspaper endorsements, information on House and Senate races, and other extras.

7:58 a.m. -- Busy signals at the official campaign Web sites for Clinton (http://www.cg96.org) and Dole (http://www.dole96.com/), are the first signs of heavy traffic that will plague election Web sites throughout the day.

8 a.m. -- Traffic jams are absent at Ross Perot's virtual campaign headquarters (http://www.perot.org), where there's no live news, but a last-ditch plea to help "Make History Tuesday" by giving Perot's Reform Party 25 percent of the vote, qualifying it to receive funding on par with the two major parties.
9 a.m. -- NBC broadcasts its regular schedule of soaps, talk shows and local news until 3 p.m.
10:24 a.m. -- Dole/Kemp campaign headquarters ask voters to "Choose honesty and integrity ... Choose Bob Dole," and follows up with campaign headlines from the previous day.

12:15 p.m. -- The Clinton Web site puts on its Election Day face, offering an "I Voted Election 96" icon for people to paste onto their personal Web pages, comments from Clinton supporters and a promise of state-by-state presidential election results once polls close.
12:45 p.m. -- AllPolitics (http://allpolitics.com/), the CNN-Time joint campaign news venture, is ready for action, offering news and returns for presidential, Congressional and gubernatorial races.
3 p.m. -- No change on PoliticsNow, Clinton, Dole or Perot Web sites. NBC's local affiliate in Los Angeles comes on the air with coverage of local races and a story on voter apathy.

4 p.m. -- NBC's "Decision 96" telecast begins, starting with results of several East Coast races. Anchor Tom Brokaw reminds viewers they can get more details on MSNBC (http://www.msnbc.com/), but the Web site for the network's online news joint venture with Microsoft is bogged down by election-hungry net surfers, making it impossible to visit.

As polls close on the East Coast, AllPolitics projects a Clinton win in Florida and displays a map of electoral college votes. News Web sites, including Yahoo (http://www.yahoo.com/), the Web search directory, start posting hot links to election coverage.
5 p.m. -- Busy signals at PoliticsNow and MSNBC. Polls close in 17 states.
5:45 p.m. -- Initial NBC tallies give Clinton 212 electoral votes, Dole 35.

6 p.m. -- Busy signals continue at PoliticsNow and MSNBC from cities such as Los Angeles and Chicago. AllPolitics sees Clinton "edging ever closer to a second term," with 212 electoral votes, 75 for Dole.

6:05 p.m. -- NBC cameras cut to a glum group of Dole campaign workers in a buffet dinner line in Russell, Kan., as the results ticker counts off 275 electoral votes for Clinton, five more than he needs to win. A half hour later, the network cuts to Tony Bennett crooning at an early Democrat victory party.

6:44 p.m. -- AllPolitics declares Clinton the winner. The news is the same at MSNBC -- accessible at last, while traffic jams continue on PoliticsNow. The official Clinton Web site offers state-by-state results but no proclamation of victory, while the official Dole and Perot sites haven't been updated since morning.

7:30 p.m. -- NBC gives the race to Clinton, as network news cameras scan a celebratory crowd in Little Rock, Ark., where the president will later give his victory speech. A few minutes later, third-place finisher Ross Perot addresses supporters, promising to "keep the pressure on the major issues."

8 p.m. -- Polls close in California. NBC gives Clinton 49 percent of the popular vote, Dole 41 percent. At PoliticsNow -- accessible for the first time in hours -- political pundits are online taking questions and analysing results. AllPolitics continues to update returns in senate and state races. Official campaign sites for Clinton, Dole and Perot still haven't been updated.
8:30 p.m. -- NBC has Dole live as he concedes the election.
(Michelle V. Rafter writes about cyberspace and technology from Los Angeles. Reach her at mvrafter(at)deltanet.com. Opinions expressed in this column are her own.)
